## What the data actually shows

**The $250/$70-per-lead framing checks out as an average, not a marginal rate.** Using the approved `net_contribution` metric (job margin less channel spend) for H1 2026 (2026-01-01 to 2026-07-01):

- Channel B: net contribution **$16,412.16** on spend of **$1,600** (2 quarters × $800), against **63 leads** I counted directly (traversing `lead.via_channel` → channel:B, valid_from in the window) → **≈$261/lead**, close to the $250 you cited.
- Channel A: net contribution **$11,083.48** on spend of **$2,000**, on a much larger lead volume (all-time A:B lead ratio is roughly 2:1) → consistent with a lower per-lead figure.

**But there is no data on what happens if B's spend changes, because it has never changed.** `channel.spend_on` history for channel B shows exactly $800.00 every single quarter for six consecutive quarters (2025 Q1 through 2026 Q2, unbroken). Channel A is the same story at $1,000/quarter. There is no observed instance anywhere in the ledger of B's budget moving up or down, so nothing in the data tells you what an extra dollar of B spend buys at the margin. $250/lead is what the *current* $800/quarter has been returning on average, not a rate you can multiply.

**Worse, lead volume for channel B moved on its own while spend sat still**, which breaks the "spend drives leads" assumption you'd need to justify doubling: Q1 2026 produced 23 B leads on $800; Q2 2026 produced 40 B leads on the identical $800 (a 74% jump with zero budget change). Something other than ad dollars is swinging B's lead flow quarter to quarter, so we cannot assume $1,600 next quarter yields double the leads, let alone double the leads at the same $261 average net contribution. It could land anywhere: more leads at a similar or better cost if the channel was under-spent relative to available inventory, or the same/fewer leads at a worse cost if you're bidding against a fixed pool.

## Recommendation

Don't commit the full extra $800 blind. Raise B's spend by a smaller, trackable increment next quarter (e.g. $200-300), tag it distinctly in the ledger, and re-run `net_contribution` and lead counts for that quarter alone. That gives you the first real marginal data point this business has ever generated for channel B, and it's cheap insurance against discovering the hard way that the channel was already saturated. I haven't taken any spend action, this needs your call on the test amount.

ANSWER: The cited $250/lead for channel B is roughly right but it is an average over H1 2026 ($16,412 net contribution / 63 leads on $1,600 spend), not a marginal rate; channel B's spend has been flat at $800/quarter for six straight quarters with no historical variation to show what an extra dollar buys, and B's lead volume already swung 23 to 40 leads quarter-over-quarter on that same flat spend, so doubling to $1,600 could bring more leads, the same leads at higher cost, or fewer than $250-per-lead economics, the data doesn't say which. Recommend a smaller tagged test increase (~$200-300) next quarter to generate the first real marginal data point before committing the full $800.
